questions.question: When designing a matrix approximation experiment with random orthogonal targets, what is the primary reason to use orthogonal matrices as targets?
questions.choice_A: They have well-controlled singular values, isolating structural expressivity from conditioning effects
questions.choice_B: They minimize Frobenius norm error by construction for any approximator
questions.choice_C: They guarantee perfect approximation by any low-rank parameterization
questions.choice_D: They eliminate the need for multiple random seeds

questions.question: Which property distinguishes the spectral norm error from the Frobenius norm error when evaluating matrix approximations?
questions.choice_A: The spectral norm averages errors across all entries
questions.choice_B: The spectral norm emphasizes the worst-case amplification along any direction
questions.choice_C: The Frobenius norm is invariant to orthogonal transformations while the spectral norm is not
questions.choice_D: The Frobenius norm upper-bounds the spectral norm for any matrix

questions.question: In angle-based metrics for approximation quality, what does a small principal angle between the approximate and target subspaces indicate?
questions.choice_A: The approximator has matched the target’s singular values but not its singular vectors
questions.choice_B: Training was unstable and suffered from exploding gradients
questions.choice_C: The approximator captures the target’s dominant subspace directions well
questions.choice_D: The approximation error in Frobenius norm must be near zero

questions.question: Why is it important to control the total number of trainable parameters when performing ablation studies on block sizes and stages in structured parameterizations?
questions.choice_A: To ensure the model’s training time remains constant
questions.choice_B: To avoid changing the optimizer’s effective learning rate
questions.choice_C: To maximize the likelihood of converging to a global optimum
questions.choice_D: To attribute improvements to structure rather than capacity

questions.question: Which experimental design choice best isolates the expressivity of a structured parameterization from optimization dynamics?
questions.choice_A: Evaluate approximation error on a fixed set of targets without further fine-tuning
questions.choice_B: Increase the batch size until the loss plateaus
questions.choice_C: Use a larger learning rate to speed convergence
questions.choice_D: Stop training early to limit overfitting

questions.question: What is the main advantage of reporting confidence intervals over reporting single-run metrics in matrix approximation experiments?
questions.choice_A: Confidence intervals guarantee that the mean error will decrease with more data
questions.choice_B: They quantify uncertainty due to randomness in initialization and data sampling
questions.choice_C: They eliminate the need to report the number of runs
questions.choice_D: They correct for biases introduced by hyperparameter tuning

questions.question: When comparing PEFT methods (e.g., LoRA vs. adapters) on a common benchmark, what is the most appropriate baseline to ensure a fair comparison of expressivity?
questions.choice_A: A fully fine-tuned model with twice the parameters
questions.choice_B: An untrained model with random weights
questions.choice_C: A parameter-matched low-rank or sparse baseline with equivalent trainable parameter count
questions.choice_D: A distilled student model with fewer layers

questions.question: Which visualization most directly reveals patterns of enforced sparsity and information flow in a structured parameterization?
questions.choice_A: Learning rate schedules over epochs
questions.choice_B: Validation loss curves across seeds
questions.choice_C: Singular value histograms of weight matrices
questions.choice_D: Heatmaps of nonzero entries and block connectivity graphs

questions.question: Why might spectral norm error be a more stringent measure than Frobenius norm error for safety-critical applications?
questions.choice_A: It penalizes diffuse errors more than localized ones
questions.choice_B: It emphasizes average-case rather than worst-case behavior
questions.choice_C: It captures the maximum gain the approximation can induce along any direction
questions.choice_D: It is invariant to changes in the target matrix

questions.question: In reporting approximation results, why is it recommended to fix and publish random seeds or seed-generation protocols?
questions.choice_A: To ensure identical convergence path across all optimizers
questions.choice_B: To enhance reproducibility by allowing others to regenerate the same randomized targets and initializations
questions.choice_C: To remove the need for multiple experimental runs
questions.choice_D: To guarantee non-overlapping confidence intervals between methods

questions.question: What does a large gap between training-set approximation error and held-out target approximation error most likely indicate in the context of expressivity experiments?
questions.choice_A: Underparameterization of the approximator
questions.choice_B: Perfect generalization due to strong inductive bias
questions.choice_C: Overfitting to the specific targets or initialization artifacts
questions.choice_D: Numerical stability of the optimizer

questions.question: Which practice most reliably separates the effect of block size from total parameter count in an ablation?
questions.choice_A: Vary block size and allow parameter count to change freely
questions.choice_B: Fix block size and vary depth arbitrarily
questions.choice_C: Match total trainable parameters across configurations while sweeping block sizes
questions.choice_D: Compare each configuration to a different baseline each time

questions.question: What is a key reason to include random orthogonal targets of varying dimensions when measuring expressivity?
questions.choice_A: To ensure that the approximation error is identical across sizes
questions.choice_B: To probe scaling behavior and sensitivity to dimensionality
questions.choice_C: To avoid the need for normalization in error metrics
questions.choice_D: To make angle-based metrics unnecessary

questions.question: When summarizing results across multiple random targets, which statistical reporting choice best communicates both central tendency and variability?
questions.choice_A: Minimum error over runs
questions.choice_B: Median with interquartile range or mean with 95% confidence interval
questions.choice_C: Single best seed
questions.choice_D: Number of epochs until convergence

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the trade-off between expressivity and generalization for structured parameterizations in approximation experiments?
questions.choice_A: Higher expressivity always yields better generalization on new targets
questions.choice_B: Lower expressivity guarantees robustness to distribution shifts
questions.choice_C: Increased expressivity reduces inductive bias and can hurt generalization without proper regularization
questions.choice_D: Expressivity and generalization are independent and should be studied separately

questions.question: Why might angle-based metrics be preferred when comparing approximations that target subspaces (e.g., top-$k$ principal components) rather than full matrices?
questions.choice_A: Angles directly quantify alignment between subspaces irrespective of scaling
questions.choice_B: Angles are easier to optimize with gradient descent
questions.choice_C: Angles can only decrease during training, ensuring monotonic improvement
questions.choice_D: Angles subsume spectral and Frobenius norms

questions.question: In a PEFT benchmarking suite, which baseline helps isolate the contribution of task data versus architectural structure?
questions.choice_A: A frozen backbone with random adapters of matched size evaluated without training
questions.choice_B: A fully fine-tuned model trained on an unrelated dataset
questions.choice_C: A larger backbone trained with early stopping
questions.choice_D: A model trained with label smoothing

questions.question: Which methodological choice best improves the repeatability of approximation experiments across laboratories?
questions.choice_A: Using proprietary datasets for stronger results
questions.choice_B: Publishing complete experiment manifests, including seeds, data preprocessing, and hyperparameters
questions.choice_C: Reducing the number of runs to lower variance
questions.choice_D: Relying solely on default optimizer settings

questions.question: What is a potential pitfall of comparing structured parameterizations solely by final training loss without capacity controls?
questions.choice_A: It overestimates the role of initialization schemes
questions.choice_B: It underestimates the impact of learning rate warmup
questions.choice_C: It may conflate expressivity gains with increased parameter count
questions.choice_D: It ignores the effect of regularization on optimization speed

questions.question: When visualizing sparsity patterns, what additional diagnostic can clarify how information flows through multi-stage structures?
questions.choice_A: Confusion matrices
questions.choice_B: Per-layer gradient norms over training
questions.choice_C: Directed acyclic graphs showing inter-block dependencies and path lengths
questions.choice_D: Receiver operating characteristic curves

questions.question: Which practice helps ensure that reported confidence intervals for approximation error are statistically sound when distributional assumptions are unclear?
questions.choice_A: Assuming normality and using parametric t-intervals with any sample size
questions.choice_B: Reporting only standard errors without intervals
questions.choice_C: Using nonparametric bootstrapping over targets or seeds
questions.choice_D: Reporting the smallest interval observed across methods
